chapter.title: Wes
chapter.sub: Forty rooms of remote students hear themselves a third of a second late. The preset was Wes's. What happens next is Maya's.

items.text: SEASON 5 · EPISODE 5 · DRAFT  Mentoring · Maya, Wes, Nadia and Farah · Level L4 · Intermediate support  Friday, first period. In forty hybrid classrooms, remote students hear their own voices a third of a second late. Last night Wes pushed a better preset — with one click, and no change record.  ⚑ RV-129: echo cancellation simplified. RV-124: mistakes shown with care. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: Wes
items.stakes: Forty rooms of remote students hear their own voices a third of a second late. The preset was Wes's. What happens next is Maya's.
items.clock: Before the 11:00 class change — and before Monday's review.
items.reward: Forty clean rooms. Hall B's loop back. Wes still telling you things next time.

objectives.text: Find out what v7 really changed
Roll back without breaking Hall B
Look closer: two things about Thursday night

items.rumor: The preset was better. That's what makes this hard.

items.alt: A hybrid classroom at 9:04: the front screen shows four remote students' tiles. One remote student's words come back to her a moment later, marked ECHO 300 ms.
items.caption: Remote students hear their own voices a third of a second late. In forty rooms.

lines.text: I was going to write the change record this morning. It was a better preset. It was.
I believe you. Breathe. Then show me the diff.

items.alt: The AV office: Nadia, the AV operations manager, on the phone by the tile wall; Wes at his desk, pale.

bubbles.text: Forty hybrid rooms reporting echo since nine. What changed last night?

items.prompt: (quietly) Are you going to tell her it was me?

options.label: “I'm going to tell her it was us. Our process let one click reach forty rooms.”
options.reply: …Okay. Okay. Then I'm writing the timeline.

options.label: “She'll find out anyway.”
options.reply: Right. Yeah. (He doesn't say anything else for an hour.)

options.label: “What do you think you should tell her?”
options.reply: That I pushed it. And that I don't know yet what broke.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #46 · AVERY'S LENS  Blame the process, fix it together  When a person's mistake reaches users, look first at what let one person's mistake reach them.  One click reached forty rooms. The review asked why one click could — not who clicked.

items.prompt: 9:08. Nadia is on the phone: “Who pushed it?” Wes is standing right next to you.
items.risk: Wes's trust — and every remote student's morning.
timeout: You say nothing. Nadia fills the silence herself.

hints.text: What let one person's mistake reach forty rooms?

options.label: “Wes pushed it last night.”
options.result: True. Wes hears it. Nadia makes a note. Wes stops telling you things for a month.
options.consequence: Accurate, and it teaches him to hide the next one.
options.fail: Blame the person and you lose the next early warning.

options.label: “We pushed a preset without a change record. We'll fix it and own the review together.”
options.result: Nadia: “Fine. Fix it, then tell me how it won't happen again.” Wes breathes out.
options.consequence: The process let one click reach forty rooms. Own the process — with him.

options.label: “Still investigating.”
options.result: Nadia hears the pause. She finds the push log herself at 9:30.
options.consequence: Hiding costs more trust than the mistake.
options.fail: She'll find out — from someone else.

options.label: “Wes will sort it out.”
options.result: Wes, alone, starts pushing v6 to everything.
options.consequence: Leaves him alone with it — and with the next mistake.

items.alt: System View of a hybrid room on v7: the far end plays from the speakers, the ceiling mics hear the speakers through the air, and the echo canceller's reference is the local program bus — so it removes the wrong thing.
items.caption: The canceller can only remove what its reference tells it to.

items.title: Room L-02 · capture only
items.body: v7's template was cloned from L-02, a lecture-capture room with no remote participants — where a canceller referenced to the program bus does no harm. Every template carries the assumptions of the room it came from. Wes adds a line to the template header: *source room · has far end? Y/N.*

items.title: Cancelling your own voice
items.body: In the 1960s, engineers at Bell Labs worked out how to cancel echoes on long-distance telephone circuits — especially satellite links, where the round trip was long enough to make speakers stumble. Their adaptive echo canceller learned the echo path and subtracted a copy of the far-end signal. Every hybrid room's canceller still depends on the same thing: being told what the far end sounds like.

items.alt: Wes's diff of v6 against v7: better capture gain and mic EQ, marked with ticks — and the echo canceller's reference changed from the far-end receive to the program bus, marked with a cross.
items.caption: Two good changes and one bad one, in the same click.

items.title: The preset was better.
items.body: v7's capture gain and EQ really are better — faculty had complained about muddy recordings for a term. But Wes cloned it from L-02, a capture-only room with no remote participants, where the canceller's reference doesn't matter. The improvement and the defect arrived together.
items.label: Test: why roll back something that was better?

items.sub: Intermediate · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Maya and Wes beside a board. Round trip: two times the one-way delay. The far end hears its own voice after twice the path. One-way a hundred and fifty milliseconds… three hundred back to them. That's the echo they heard. And the canceller only removes what its reference tells it to. Your preset moved the reference.

items.text: 📗 FIELD NOTES · INTERMEDIATE  Terms   Echo cancellation   Reference signal   Change record   Formula and variables   ƒ FORMULA · Round-trip delay  t echo  = 2 × t one-way    t one-way   delay in one direction     ƒ FORMULA · Echo distance (there and back)  d = c × t ÷ 2   d  one-way distance to the reflector, m  c  speed of sound, about 343 m/s in air at 20 °C  t  echo delay, s

items.label: **Learn it now:** echo cancellation and its reference.

Act II — “One room at a time”

items.alt: Hall B, the lecture hall with the hearing loop fixed on Tuesday. Farah on the phone, the loop sign behind her.

bubbles.text: Hall B's loop is quiet again. Mira's in row ten. What happened?

items.title: Hall B.
items.body: v7 didn't only change forty rooms' echo cancellers. It carried every room's local settings too — and reset Hall B's hearing-loop feed, fixed on Tuesday, to the preset's default. A global rollback to v6 would reset it again: v6 is older than Tuesday.
items.label: Test: why not push v6 everywhere?

items.prompt: 9:30. How do you get forty rooms back?
items.happening: Echo in forty rooms; Hall B loop reset.
items.risk: Breaking Hall B twice in a week.
timeout: Wes pushes v6 everywhere while you think.
Hall B's loop goes quiet again.

hints.text: What undo does each room already have?

options.label: Push v6 to all forty rooms in one click
options.result: The echo stops at 9:32. Hall B's loop feed is reset — again — to v6's default.
options.consequence: One click caused it; one click repeats it.

options.label: Restore pilot room B-114 from its own nightly snapshot and make a test call; then the rest in batches of ten from each room's own snapshot
options.result: B-114: no echo. Batch by batch: clean. Hall B's loop comes back with its own snapshot.
options.consequence: Each room gets its own undo, proven one room first.

options.label: Tell faculty to mute the room speakers
options.result: No echo — and the room can't hear the remote students at all.

options.label: Leave it until the weekend
options.result: Two more days of remote students hearing themselves.
options.consequence: Too long for people in class now.

items.alt: Pilot room B-114: Wes on the remote test account through his headset; Maya at the lectern speaking a test sentence.

bubbles.text: I only hear the room. No me.
One room. Now the next ten — and a call for each.

lines.text: Hall B's loop is quiet again. Tuesday's fix — gone. What happened?
We did. It's coming back with the room's own snapshot, not a global one. Ten minutes.

items.label: **Fix it:** give the echo canceller the right reference — for v8.

items.happening: All forty rooms clean. Hall B restored.
known: ◉ Local settings lived in the global preset
items.risk: The same Friday, with someone else's click.
timeout: The review ends without a change.
The gap stays open for the next person.

hints.text: What let it happen — and who else could it happen to?

options.label: Change records for every preset, a pilot and a test call before batches, room-specific settings kept out of global presets — and reviews both ways: Wes reviews Maya's next change
options.result: Wes reviews Maya's firmware plan on Wednesday and finds a room she missed.
options.consequence: Fix the system that let one click reach forty rooms — and make review a habit, not a punishment.

options.label: Take Wes's push rights away
options.result: He stops making improvements. So does everyone watching.
options.consequence: Punishes the person, keeps the gap.
options.fail: The next person with rights has the same gap.

options.label: Freeze all preset changes this term
options.result: Muddy recordings for four more months.
options.consequence: Stops the good changes with the bad.

options.label: Maya approves every change herself
options.result: Maya becomes the bottleneck for 400 rooms.
options.consequence: One reviewer is a single point of failure.

items.label: **Sequence:** push a preset you can stand behind.

items.alt: System View on v8: the canceller's reference is the far-end audio — exactly what the speakers play — so it removes it before the mics' sound goes back to the remote students.
items.caption: v8: v7's better levels, and the right reference. Piloted, tested, reviewed.

items.alt: The AV office after the review. Wes and Maya by the window; a chipped mug on Maya's desk.

bubbles.text: Why didn't you just tell her it was me?
Because it was us. Someone said that for me once. Now write me a better change record than I would.

items.title: A mug that says RAY
items.body: On Maya's desk: a chipped mug that says RAY. In her first year at the church she broke a Sunday service with a change nobody had checked. Ray told the pastor, “We did.” Then he made her write the timeline. She kept the mug.

items.alt: A lecture hall. Professor Grant, gray-bearded, stands at the whiteboard far from the lectern.

bubbles.text: My lecture recordings sound as though I leave the room every ten minutes. For three years I've been told the microphones are fine.

items.caption: Next: *Professor Grant.*

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  An echo canceller removes what its reference tells it to: in a hybrid room, the far end. Push presets through a record, a pilot room, a test call and batches, keep room settings out of global presets — and when a mistake reaches people, fix the process that let it.
REFLECTION (optional)  · Maya said “we” when it was Wes who clicked. When has someone taken shared responsibility for your mistake — and what did it change?
